observation.visible_scene: A sunlit scrubland hillside: a dirt track runs diagonally up the slope, a lichen-mottled rock sits mid-frame, surrounded by grass tufts, low shrubs and thin bare tree trunks. A bright diagonal sun streak / lens flare enters from the upper left throughout.
visible_changes: The lens flare changes character over the segment: it begins as a pale white diagonal streak (frames 1-8), blooms into a strong magenta/pink multi-ray flare washing the upper-left of the frame (frames 9-25), then fades back toward a white streak (frames 26-41). This is a reflection artifact, not a physical object moving in the scene.

Handheld camera drift: comparing the first and last frames, the rock and the left grass tuft shift position within the frame (rock moves slightly up-left, tuft moves toward the left edge), indicating a slow pan/tilt of the camera rather than movement of the plants or rock themselves.
The vegetation, rock and dirt track are otherwise stationary; no object translation, deformation or occlusion is visible.
Minor handheld jitter/shake is present frame-to-frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the flare intensity change (sun angle, a hand or object passing near the lens, or cloud movement) is not shown.
Whether any wind-induced plant motion occurs is not evident within this segment.
Events before the first frame and after the last frame are unknown.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and magnitude of camera motion (pan vs tilt vs roll) is hard to pin down because the background is featureless scrub.
The flare is a lens reflection and should not be read as a separate scene element.
